source:
Hana: I think we should delay the launch until the load test passes at five thousand concurrent users.
Marco: Waiting another month costs us the holiday window. Ship at three thousand and patch if it buckles.
Hana: A failed launch window is worse than a missed one. Outages during peak season become our reputation.
Marco: Reputation does not pay salaries. Three thousand covers our forecast peak with margin.
Yusuf: I will go with whichever option keeps support tickets manageable in December.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should the launch be delayed until the load test passes at five thousand concurrent users?

positions.label: Delay until load test passes
positions.thesis: The launch should wait until the system passes the load test at five thousand concurrent users.
positions.steelman: A peak-season outage converts first-time users into detractors and costs more than a missed launch window.

groundingQuotes.quote: I think we should delay the launch until the load test passes at five thousand concurrent users.

positions.label: Ship now at three thousand
positions.thesis: The team should ship now at three thousand concurrent users and patch if problems appear, because the holiday window matters more.
positions.steelman: Forecast demand fits current capacity with margin, so delay only surrenders revenue without reducing real risk.

groundingQuotes.quote: Ship at three thousand and patch if it buckles.

positions.label: Whichever keeps support manageable
positions.thesis: Yusuf prefers whichever option keeps December support tickets manageable.
positions.steelman: Support load is the operational signal that captures both outage risk and launch timing, so optimizing for it is defensible.

groundingQuotes.quote: I will go with whichever option keeps support tickets manageable in December.

claims.statement: An outage during peak season would damage the product's reputation in a way a missed window would not.

resolution.condition: Agree how to weight reputational downside against a missed sales window.

groundingQuotes.quote: A failed launch window is worse than a missed one.

claims.statement: Three thousand concurrent users covers the forecast holiday peak with margin.

resolution.condition: Validate the demand forecast against last year's peak plus growth assumptions.

groundingQuotes.quote: Three thousand covers our forecast peak with margin.

claims.statement: The launch option should be chosen to keep December support tickets manageable.

resolution.condition: Agree that support-load exposure is an acceptable tiebreaking criterion for the launch call.

groundingQuotes.quote: I will go with whichever option keeps support tickets manageable in December.

commonGroundCandidates.statement: All three participants accept that December conditions, not average days, are what the decision must survive.

groundingQuotes.quote: Outages during peak season become our reputation.
Waiting another month costs us the holiday window.

disagreementCandidates.question: Does three thousand concurrent users cover the forecast holiday peak with margin?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Marco says yes; Hana's insistence on the five-thousand test implies she does not trust the forecast margin.

participantStances.stance: Unproven until the load test passes.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Run the load test or validate the forecast against prior peaks.

disagreementCandidates.question: Should a possible outage weigh more heavily than a missed holiday window?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Hana weights reputational downside above timing; Marco weights the certain cost of delay above speculative outage harm.

participantStances.stance: Outage damage outweighs missing the window.
Reputation does not pay salaries; the missed window is certain.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Leadership decides the risk tradeoff explicitly.

caveats: Yusuf's position is inferred from a stated criterion, not an explicit launch recommendation.
